title: BAGMAN GovernedEntity
description: Canonical `GovernedEntity` (PID §4). A governed entity is a stable BAGMAN identity (e.g. NOUSTAI_LIMITED, INFOSECURS_LIMITED, MATTHEW_SCOTT_PERSONAL) that must not depend on email address, bank account, Xero tenant, legal registration number, display name, or current jurisdiction — those may be associated with the entity later. Every canonical financial or evidential record must ultimately be associated with exactly one governed entity, or be explicitly unresolved (see `entity_id` on `EvidenceItem`); unresolved is a first-class state, never a silent inference.

entity_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this entity. Immutable once assigned: once an `entity_id` has been issued for a governed entity it must never be reassigned or changed for the life of that entity. JSON Schema validates the shape of a single instance only and cannot itself enforce immutability across time/writes — that guarantee is enforced at the domain/repository layer (e.g. an EntityRepository rejecting any update that changes `entity_id`), not by this schema.

entity_type.description: The kind of governed entity. Deliberately open (NOT a closed enum) so new entity types can be introduced without a schema redesign, per PID §4's explicit extensibility requirement. Known initial values (documentation only, not an enforced closed set): `COMPANY`, `PERSON`. Anticipated future values include `TRUST`, `PARTNERSHIP`, `OTHER`.

canonical_name.description: Stable, human-legible slug identifier for the entity, e.g. `NOUSTAI_LIMITED`. Distinct from `entity_id` (the opaque internal identifier — never business-meaningful) and from `display_name` (a human-friendly label that may change over time). `canonical_name` is expected to remain stable but is a legible business-facing slug, not the opaque canonical ID.

display_name.description: Human-friendly display label for the entity, e.g. "Noustai Limited". May change over time; not used as a canonical identifier.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the governed entity. Deliberately open (NOT a closed enum), for the same extensibility reason as `entity_type`. Known initial values (documentation only): `ACTIVE`, `ARCHIVED`.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp at which this entity was registered in BAGMAN.

fiscal_year_start_month_day.description: CD-6 architect amendment (email historical-ingestion boundary). The RECURRING month-day (MM-DD, always UTC-calendar) on which this entity's accounting/financial year starts in every FUTURE year, e.g. `"11-01"` for a 1 November fiscal year start, `"04-06"` for the UK personal tax year. This is the field a caller actually derives the real historical-ingestion bootstrap boundary FROM (see `services.mailbox.bootstrap_policy.compute_entity_historical_bootstrap`) — `historical_floor_override_at` below is only ever an optional clamp on that derivation, never the answer itself. Required key, explicit `null` when this configuration is not yet known for a given entity (never invented, never silently defaulted) — a `null` here is a real, actionable 'missing configuration' state a caller must surface, not an oversight.

historical_floor_override_at.description: CD-6 architect amendment (email historical-ingestion boundary), RENAMED from `email_bootstrap_floor_at` after a real conceptual-conflation bug: the OLD name and its old description wrongly treated this as 'the definitive literal historical-bootstrap date'. It is not, and never should have been — it is an OPTIONAL CLAMP/OVERRIDE only. The real historical-ingestion bootstrap boundary is DERIVED (start of the previous COMPLETED accounting period, computed from `fiscal_year_start_month_day` + 'now' — see `services.mailbox.bootstrap_policy.compute_entity_historical_bootstrap`), and this field, when set to a real commencement/incorporation date, simply ensures that derivation never predates it (e.g. NoustAI Limited's 2025-12-05 incorporation date, which the naive '1 January' rule applied alone would otherwise predate). `null` is the correct, common, and entirely PERMANENT state for most entities (e.g. a company incorporated long before any of this matters, or a person) — it means 'no override needed, trust the period-derivation alone', never 'not yet configured'. `fiscal_year_start_month_day` being `null` is the real 'missing configuration' signal `services.mailbox.sweep.compute_bootstrap_floor` refuses to run without; this field being `null` never blocks a sweep on its own.

metadata.description: Free-form, genuinely open metadata about the entity. Additional properties are intentionally permitted here (unlike the top level of this schema) per the PID's own metadata examples. Must not contain secrets or sensitive company/account data (PID §23, §29).
